programmes.d: Can a fighter jet gear box help Ishy Khan win this leg of the road trip?
It's day two and experts David Barby and Margie Cooper are battling it out in County Durham before winding their way to the auction in Scarborough.

Claire Rawle finds out about the Tynemouth Volunteer Life Brigade and Paul Laidlaw visits a military observation post in Blyth. And Paul finds some RAF stereoscopic aerial reconnaissance photographs of German U-boats at a great price.
Final finds include a French mantel clock and Chinese bellows.
David Barby and Margie Cooper embark on day three of the road trip from Bridlington to Sheffield, and on their way they buy some surprising items.

Claire Rawle discovers the history of big game fishing in the 1930s, while Paul Laidlaw sets off to rendezvous in a secret WWII bunker. Paul buys a pair of Charles Barlow vases, and Claire picks up an early 20th-century spectacle case.
Silver spoons and a Victorian Egyptian fob bring drama to the saleroom!
On the fourth day of their antiques road trip David Barby and Margie Cooper make some brave buys as they head for the auction in Nottingham.

Paul Laidlaw finds a rare 18th-century puzzle jug, and Claire Rawle some Shelley porcelain. Paul discovers how Hull was vital to thousands of Jews fleeing from Tsarist Russia and Claire indulges her passion for all things railway.
Margie and Tim discover Tai Chi in Liverpool before their auction battle commences.
It's the final day for David Barby and Margie Cooper as they battle it out at the last auction in Lincoln.

In the final, Paul Laidlaw hopes a late 17th-century hand-forged halberd head will earn him a huge profit. Claire Rawle buys a Chinese cloisonné vase and an Edwardian inkstand. Will Claire be the comeback kid and crush the mighty Laidlaw?
Can 100-year-old recipe books cook up a win for one expert at auction?
It's antiques experts James Braxton and Charles Hanson's turn to hit the road in a classic car, hunting for bargains on a grand trip from Somerset across to the Isle of Wight and down to Cornwall.
It's a Welsh road trip for Kate Bliss and Paul Laidlaw. Some fake currency and a leg of mutton could cause problems for our pair of antiquers at a Somerset auction.
Seagull attack caught on camera! But who will steal an auction win?
James Braxton and Charles Hanson are heading across the Solent to the Isle of Wight in search of bargains, and Charles finds a bit of history.
Psychic sketches and an obelisk turn up at Margie and Tim’s final auction slamdown.
Kate Bliss and Paul Laidlaw forage for antiques across the West Country in a stylish 1960s Volvo. Paul's fortunes rest on a treasure from Africa while Kate blows a very, very big horn.
James Braxton and Charles Hanson are battling it out along the Dorset and Devon coast--and there's a big surprise at the auction in Torquay.
Raj and Hettie’s first outing, featuring the opportunity of a lifetime!
It's day four and James Braxton and Charles Hanson are heading for Cornwall, where Charles has an enchanting experience and James goes to the fair.

Paul Laidlaw resorts to tank warfare to crush Kate Bliss's chances of profit. Kate finds out about a decisive naval confrontation while Paul heads to Southampton to discover how Britain's landscape has been mapped for generations.
Raj and Hettie get dazzled by jewels in Norfolk.
James Braxton and Charles Hanson head deep into Cornwall on the last day of their road trip. James goes to church before the final auction in Truro.

Paul Laidlaw and Kate Bliss hope to capitalize on some risky buys. Paul believes a strange collection of medals will honor him with profits, but will a pricey three-figure gamble purchase pay off for Kate?
Wooden stilts, Derbyshire Blue John and the shocking story of the Witch Finder General!
It's a new road trip! Anita Manning and Philip Serrell are touring the north of England in their classic car, aiming for a profit in Edinburgh.

Kate Bliss and Paul Laidlaw's final trip sees them through Kent. At an incredible auction in Bury St. Edmunds, the Antiques Road Trip record profit is truly smashed, and when the gavel finally goes down one expert is left close to tears.
Art deco penguin cocktail shaker vs. a soapstone Inuit carving!
As Anita Manning and Philip Serrell head to auction in County Durham, Philip develops an odd interest in sewing and Anita eyes up a wedding dress.

Christina Trevanion and James Braxton are in the Scottish Borders with a '60s Jaguar. James resorts to a flashlight as he rummages in the dark for an occasional table while Christina hopes some silver-plated cutlery will serve up a profit.
An anatomical eye model and old rugby ball go head-to-head in this final auction.
Anita Manning and Philip Serrell get the bit between their teeth as they head through the Dales and make the most of its horse racing history.

Christina Trevanion and James Braxton's are in the cold and snowy Trossachs. James investigates some ancient treasures in a Glasgow graveyard and farmer's wife Christina learns why it was the Scots who transformed arable farming.
Flamboyant besties Roo and Mark go head-to-head in Yorkshire.
On day four of their trip Anita Manning and Philip Serrell head for the bright lights of Blackpool and can't resist a visit to the pleasure beach.
Mark takes on Roo and swoons over a rare find.

Christina Trevanion and James Braxton start in Levenshulme, Manchester. James has the unusual problem of having too much cash, while Christina struggles with her limited funds, deciding to gamble them on a worn toy train.
Anita Manning and Philip Serrell go head-to-head at an auction in Harrogate on this final day of their road trip.
A car-shaped teapot and art nouveau vase race to auction, but who will ring in profits?

The seaside town of Southport in Merseyside is Christina Trevanion and James Braxton's next stop. Christina dibs her way to a purchase with a Scouting connection and James spends a vast amount of his cash on two Cantonese jardinières.
Experts Mark Stacey and Mark Hales battle it out in the auction rooms and antiques shops of eastern England in a race to turn an unbeatable profit.
Will Mark’s rare piece of glass beat Roo at auction?
In the battle of the two Marks, Mark Stacey and Mark Hales make some surprising investments as they make their way from Rutland to Norfolk.

In Whitley Bay, Christina Trevanion and James Braxton set off on their finale. Christina buys a Chinese silver bowl and James has found six Japanese porcelain teacups. After their buying spree, they head to Ayr for a memorable auction.
Can a glass dog beat a lion head in this final auction of the trip?
On the third day of their road trip Mark Stacey visits the magnificent Ely Cathedral and his opponent Mark Hales gets excited about a sketchbook.

Phil Serrell is joined by new Road Tripper Arusha Irvine on a jaunt around Herefordshire's antique shops in a 1976 Triumph Stag. Phil's joined by Daphne, his dog, while Roo finds a 300-year-old example of Georgian glass.
Our jewelry experts go awol with a wooden donkey block and fairy money box!
Road trippers Mark Stacey and Mark Hales head for East Anglia in their classic car as the battle to win intensifies between them.
Road Trip regular, Phil Serrell, plays a safe bet with a mahogany breakfast table, while Arusha 'Roo' Irvine's all at sea, gambling on an antique pond yacht.
Ishy may have found the world’s biggest pencil, but will anyone buy it?
In this final day of their 300-mile road trip, Mark Hales gets a lesson in spying and Mark Stacey is left stunned at the auction.

Roo Irvine and Phil Serrell explore Yorkshire and Derbyshire. Along the way they dig up coal mining musical history, Phil attempts to buy a horse and Roo picks up another piece of her favorite glassware.
Lobsters, lizards and a silver duck are discovered deep in Gloucestershire!
It's time for Thomas Plant and James Lewis to take their classic car bargain hunting around the highlands and lowlands of Scotland.
Catherine and Ishy get their hands on centuries old plasticine!

Phil Serrell and Roo Irvine explore Oxfordshire. However, will the Stratford upon Avon auction supply comedy, tragedy or both? Plus, how the Chipping Norton Scouts re-invented British baseball and the Queen of 19th-century science.
Experts Thomas Plant and James Lewis pick up some very unusual items as they travel across Scotland from west to east coast in their classic car.
Our duo walk in the footsteps of dinosaurs, uncovering the oldest find of the trip.

As Roo Irvine and Phil Serrell motor through the Cotswolds, Phil picks up a Victorian marmalade cutter, while Roo hopes a 16th-century bronze thimble will earn her a big profit. But who will be victorious at the final auction in Newent?
Thomas Plant takes a financial gamble and James Lewis talks to animals on the third leg of their trip around Scotland.
A hot rod, two experts and a boot full of antiques….let the battle commence!
There's more car trouble for experts Thomas Plant and James Lewis on the fourth leg of their tour of Scotland.

Antique experts Christina Trevanion and Paul Laidlaw kick off a new season in Suffolk and Cambridgeshire. Armed with £200 each, and an ailing pickup truck, they shop up a storm before heading to an auction in Market Harborough.
Phil and Natasha scour Scotland, but can a mannequin head outclass wooden oars?
In the final leg of their trip Thomas Plant trades four wheels for two and James Lewis gets to the root of popular New Year's anthem Auld Lang Syne.
Antiques hunters Christina Trevanion and Paul Laidlaw shop across Gloucestershire and Northamptonshire before going head-to-head at an auction in Evesham, Worcestershire.
In a Road Trip first, Phil is so impressed he pays more than the ticket price!

Charlie Ross and Catherine Southon to hit the road in their classic car on a 200-mile journey to out-buy each other and outdo each other at auction. They begin in Corsham in the heart of Wiltshire and finish with an auction in Devizes.

Travelling through Hertfordshire, Buckinghamshire, and the West Midlands, Paul Laidlaw uncovers a hidden gem that could win him the trip. All is revealed when he and Christina Trevanion auction their lots in Nantwich, Cheshire.
Natasha goes glassy eyed for a tiny glass, while it’s ‘TIMBER’ for Phil.
It's day two for Charlie Ross and Catherine Southon as they cosy up on their rain-swept journey criss-crossing southern England in the hunt for antiques to sell at an auction in Wareham, Dorset.
Phil and Natasha go all out in this final auction duel!

Christina Trevanion and Paul Laidlaw travel through Shropshire and Worcestershire. Paul gets security clearance to visit Iron Mountain and Christina learns about the origins of the modern Olympic movement in Much Wenlock.
Day three of their jaunt finds Catherine Southon and Charlie Ross wending their way along the south coast, headed for a shock at the auction in Lewes.
Danny Sebastian buckles up for his first road trip taking on veteran Irita Marriott.

Paul Laidlaw and Christina Trevanion are taking in the delights of Staffordshire and Cheshire. Paul has had amazing success on this trip; can Christina catch up as they head towards their final auction in Northwich?
As Charlie Ross and Catherine Southon battle it out on day four, they take in some history on their trip from the south coast of England to London.
Saddle up for with rookie Danny versus veteran Irita in the Wild West…of England.
Antiques experts David Harper and Anita Manning go head-to-head as they road trip through North England and into southern and central Scotland, heading to an auction in Knutsford, Cheshire.
